content.text:
`/electron/init-oauth-proxy` now forwards each cookie from the inner sign-in response as its own `Set-Cookie` header, in the order the inner response emitted them. The new test passes. I didn't run the rest of the electron test suite or `pnpm typecheck`; I only ran `tsc --noEmit` on the electron package, which was clean.

The change is in `packages/electron/src/routes.ts`. It now reads the inner cookies with `getSetCookie()` and appends them one at a time, instead of collecting them into one comma-joined string. The forwarded values are the inner response's cookie strings passed through unchanged, so attributes like `Path`, `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite`, `Max-Age`, `Expires` and `Domain` carry over as they were. The redirect path is untouched, and when the inner response sets no cookies nothing is appended.

I added `packages/electron/test/init-oauth-proxy.test.ts`. It stubs the global `fetch` to return two cookies and a redirect URL with `redirect: true`, then calls the endpoint with `asResponse: true`. It checks for a `302` with the `Location` header and exactly two `Set-Cookie` entries in order (`first.cookie=one` then `second.cookie=two`). I didn't write the CLAUDE.md-style failing-first test, so I haven't seen it fail against the old code. The test doesn't cover the attribute list or the no-cookies case.

Nothing is committed.
